for floating-point arrays\ntemplate <typename T>\nvoid print_results(const std::vector<T>& data, const char* name = \"Result\") {\n    if (data.empty()) {\n        printf(\"=== RESULTS ===\\n\");\n numNodes)] = newDist;\n                    path[idx2(j, i, numNodes)] = k;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, const }\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of nodes in the graph (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t numNodes = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line The random stream is consumed in the\n// same global order as the serial original, so every rank generates the identical graph.\nvoid initializeDistanceRows(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, const size_t numNodes,\n                            const size_t rowBegin, const size_t rowEnd,\n                            const unsigned int rangeMin, const unsigned int rangeMax) {\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n    const double range = static_cast<double>(rangeMax - rangeMin) + 1.0;\n\n    for (size_t row = 0; row < numNodes; ++row) {\n        for (size_t col = 0; col < numNodes; ++col) {\n            const unsigned int value = rangeMin + (unsigned int)(range * rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX);\n            if (row >= rowBegin && row < rowEnd) {\n                dist[(row - rowBegin) * numNodes + col] = value;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Set diagonal to zero (distance from node to itself is 0)\n    for (size_t i = rowBegin; i < rowEnd; ++i) {\n        dist[(i - rowBegin) * numNodes + i] = 0;\n    }\n}\n\n// Path entries start out as their row index (same values as the serial initializePathMatrix)\n__global__ void initPathKernel(unsigned int* __restrict__ path, const size_t rows,\n                               const size_t n, const size_t rowOffset) {\n    const size_t j = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    const size_t i = blockIdx.y * blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;\n    if (i < rows && j < n) {\n        path[i * n + j] = static_cast<unsigned int>(rowOffset + i);\n    }\n}\n\n// One pivot step k applied to a block of rows. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CfxoMJKYVwGeUKeZz7q4y","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The benchmark now runs as a hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA program, and its results match the original exactly. On this machine (3× RTX 3090), n=4096 drops from 74 s to about 0.3 s.\n\n**Design**\n- **MPI:** rows are split into contiguous blocks, one per GPU worker, across ranks. Each step, the rank that owns pivot row k broadcasts it.\n- **OpenMP:** each rank runs one host thread per GPU it drives. Those threads synchronize the pivot exchange with barriers.\n- **CUDA:** one relaxation kernel per pivot step updates each GPU's rows, and an init kernel sets the path matrix.\n- **Correctness:** the random graph is generated in the original order, so every rank gets the identical graph. Row k and column k don't change during step k (the diagonal is zero and weights are non-negative), so the in-place parallel update gives the same distances and path matrix as the serial version.\n- **Output:** the format is unchanged. Only rank 0 prints. The full matrix is gathered only when `-r` or `-v` is given, and the timed region excludes gather and download, as before.\n\n**Files changed**\n- `floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp`: rewritten. The serial CPU `floydWarshall` is gone; the hybrid code replaces it.\n- `floydwarshall/CMakeLists.txt`: enables the CUDA language, finds MPI, OpenMP and CUDA, and builds the same `floydwarshall` target. It now requires CMake 3.24 for `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES native`. Host flags go through `-Xcompiler`.\n\nNo new files were created in the repo. The build was done in `/tmp`.\n\n**Verification**\n- I compared the `-r` hash, min/max, and samples against the original for `n` = 512, 1000, 37, 2, 1 across 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 ranks, three runs each. All 75 configurations matched, and validation passed.\n- I found and fixed a race during testing. The owner rank overwrote the shared pivot buffer before slower threads had finished reading it. Alternating two staging buffers removes the race without an extra barrier.\n\n**Performance (n=4096)**\n\n| Config | Time |\n|---|---|\n| Original | 74,129 ms |\n| Hybrid, 1 rank (3 GPUs) | 477 ms |\n| Hybrid, 3 ranks (1 GPU each) | 318 ms |\n\n**Limitations**\n- Each step needs one broadcast and two host-device copies, so small `n` is latency-bound. At n=512 the hybrid takes about 12–44 ms, which is still well under the original's 166 ms.\n- Path entries are computed on the GPUs and kept there. The original never printed or validated them, so they aren't exported.\n- Gathering the full matrix uses row-typed MPI counts. That supports any `n` whose row count fits in an `int`.\n\nThe next step for more speed would be a tiled blocked Floyd–Warshall to cut the per-step overhead. I haven't done that.\n\nI did not commit anything; the repo is not under git."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1054,"cache_read_input_tokens":92455,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1054},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"136cdb4f-7f69-4708-a777-4be381794db5","uuid":"57f67bef-1c68-4959-8d13-767265bfded2","timestamp":"2026-10-12T18:16:01.145Z","request_id":"req_011CfxoMHzwquPM3Z4r4V8zc"}
